text:
amar: Heads-up — kicking off capacity sims for the upcoming holiday window (two weeks). early signs show larger evening tails than our baseline, need to decide safety margins. :eyes:

jin: do we have an updated GPU-hour budget for Q3? last commit consumed ~180k GPU-hrs, forecast was 220k.

sophia: also flag: eu-west had intermittent nvlink/ucode flaps last night, added ~8% p95 tail. logs showed "nvlink error: link down" on node-92.

ben: question: are we talking about increasing steady capacity or a scheduled surge pool? different cost profiles.

amar: leaning surge pool + shorter autoscale cooldown during evening peak (22:00-02:00 local). want rough numbers first — extra GPU-hours if we add X GPUs each night?

ben: back-of-envelope: if we add 40 GPUs for 4 hours/night for 14 nights => 40 * 4 * 14 = 2240 GPU-hrs. at $2/hr that's ~$4.5k.

jin: if we set a 30% safety buffer on top of expected peak, that's another ~672 GPU-hrs (~$1.3k).

sophia: autoscaler note: we saw delay on scale-up during jitter — current cooldown is 300s. during network blips scale-up got throttled and queues ballooned. propose cooldown=90s for surge window and allow max_surge=+50%.

ben: tradeoff check: reduced cooldown increases churn and transient waste. but better than soft-fail for customer-facing latency. also suggest pre-warm prefix KV caches per-region before evening window.

amar: proposed plan: 1) create evening surge pool of 50 GPUs (region apportionment eu/us-apac split), 2) autoscale cooldown=90s for 22:00-02:00 window, 3) enable per-region prefix cache warmup 1h before window, 4) monitor p99 tokens/sec and queue length and abort if p99> threshold.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: patch "evening-surge-config" scheduled for 2026-04-08 02:00 UTC by @ben :gear:

jin: can we run Monte Carlo with worst-case: concurrent spike + 15% packet loss + longer sequences (avg seq 800) so we can see failed request distribution?

sophia: ping @eng-runtime-bot — need a 1k-run sim with jitter and region failover.

ben: starting sim now. input snippet:

```
{
  "concurrent": 48000,
  "avg_seq": 800,
  "p50_tokens_per_sec": 150000,
  "network_loss": 0.15
}
```

ben: early sim output (summary): tail failures ~1.6% -> that translates to ~768 failed requests per 48k concurrent at peak. GPU-hr impact +18% under retry pressure. more detail in the job artifact: https://ci.redwood.example/sims/1938456123

amar: ok — that's actionable. we'll move forward with surge pool + cooldown change. I'll open the PR for infra config and budget approval.

sophia: add a short runbook item: NVLink symptoms + who to page (eng-runtime oncall -> infra-hardware).

ben: PR created: #1248 — includes surge pool config, autoscaler tweak, warmup job. Also added a runbook stub in /docs/runbooks/evening-surge.md.

amar: thanks — will request finance signoff for the ~3k incremental spend and merge after approval. :thumbsup:

jin: can we also add a short dashboard panel: "evening-surge headroom" with predicted GPU-hrs and actual consumption? link to draft: https://dash.redwood.example/capacity/2026-holiday

sophia: agreed. set alert for p99 tokens/sec > 1.25x baseline and queue_len > 2500.

ben: will schedule a quick post-deploy smoke run during next staging window.

amar: perfect. thanks team.

infra-bot: note: monitoring alert created: "evening-surge-p99" -> notify #eng-oncall and #product-ops.

amar: :white_check_mark:
